predecessors.note: The Frederick V page: the Bohemian Confederacy was formed on 31 July 1619 by Bohemia, Silesia, Lusatia and Moravia. The habsburg-monarchy dossier books the loss on 19 August 1619, the Thirty Years' War page's date for the Estates withdrawing Ferdinand's election; the two dates are two acts a few weeks apart.

successors.note: After White Mountain (8 November 1620); Cliopatria returns the lands to the Habsburg Monarchy shape of 1622.

land.text: Upper and Lower Lusatia (the part of the Bohemian Crown lands that lies in Saxony and Brandenburg)

successors.note: July 1620, by the Thirty Years' War page: John George of Saxony backed Ferdinand 'in return for the cession of Lusatia'; September 1620, by the Electorate of Saxony page: Saxon troops occupied the two Lusatias for the emperor, which were pledged to Saxony in 1623 and ceded in 1636. The electorate-of-saxony dossier books the same land as a Saxon occupation for the emperor from September 1620.

capitals.name: Prague
capitals.note: The Frederick V page has him crowned in St. Vitus Cathedral in Prague on 4 November 1619 and fleeing from there to Breslau on 9 November 1620; it does not call Prague the capital, which is the researcher's reading. The Thirty Years' War page: he 'entered Prague in October 1619'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 2: Cliopatria has no row for the rebels, and its Habsburg Monarchy shape of 1619 lacks the whole Bohemian Crown. The Frederick V page names the founding lands of the Confederacy (31 July 1619): Bohemia with Silesia, Lusatia and Moravia. The cells are the lands of the Habsburg shape of 1600 that the 1619 shape no longer has, the researcher's reading. The Bohemian Revolt page adds that 'much of Upper Austria' joined the revolt; the page gives no date and the land is not drawn.

correction.text: Bohemia, Moravia and Silesia, without Lusatia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 2: the same lands without Lusatia. The Thirty Years' War page: in July 1620 John George of Saxony backed Ferdinand 'in return for the cession of Lusatia'; the Electorate of Saxony page: 'In September 1620 Saxon troops marched into the two Lusatian territories and occupied them without major resistance.' The Bohemian army is destroyed at White Mountain in November 1620, the year the state ends.

region.text: Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia, the Lands of the Bohemian Crown that Cliopatria's Habsburg Monarchy shape of 1600 holds and its shape of 1619 does not

ledger.note: 31 July 1619: the Estates of the Bohemian Crown form the Bohemian Confederacy against the Habsburgs. 'these states formed the Bohemian Confederacy, dedicated to opposing the Habsburgs'; the founding states were Bohemia with the other Lands of the Bohemian Crown, Silesia, Lusatia and Moravia. The revolt itself began earlier (the Bohemian Revolt page: on 23 May 1618 an assembly of Protestants threw the regents out of a palace window); the habsburg-monarchy dossier carries the contest from May 1618. Region is the researcher's reading of the four lands; the page does not say how much of each the Confederacy held.

region.text: Upper and Lower Lusatia (the part of the Bohemian Crown lands that lies in Saxony and Brandenburg)

ledger.note: September 1620: Saxony occupies Lusatia. The Electorate of Saxony page: 'In September 1620 Saxon troops marched into the two Lusatian territories and occupied them without major resistance', John George having agreed with Ferdinand II 'that Saxony should reconquer the two Bohemian tributary lands of Upper and Lower Lusatia for the emperor'; the lands were pledged to Saxony in 1623 and ceded in 1636. The Thirty Years' War page has only the July 1620 agreement ('John George of Saxony backed Ferdinand ... in return for the cession of Lusatia'); the Bohemian Revolt page: 'The Saxons invaded, and quickly overran most of Lusatia except for Gorlitz and Bautzen'. Reviewer eu-09-i: month moved from July to September and source moved to the Electorate of Saxony page. The electorate-of-saxony dossier books the same entry as an occupation for the emperor (counterpart habsburg-monarchy), September 1620.

region.text: Bohemia, Moravia and Silesia, without Lusatia

ledger.note: 8 November 1620: the Confederacy's army is destroyed at White Mountain. 'Ferdinand II decisively defeated Frederick V at the Battle of White Mountain, near Prague, on 8 November 1620'; the Frederick V page has him flee to Breslau on 9 November. The pages do not date the surrender of Moravia and Silesia, so the battle stands for the end of the state; Cliopatria returns the lands in 1622.

region.text: Bohemia, Moravia and Silesia, without Lusatia

ledger.note: November 1620: the Bohemian Confederacy ends with White Mountain. The Bohemian Revolt page's infobox gives the revolt as 1618-1620 and the result as an Imperial (Habsburg) victory; 'On 9 November, Frederick fled to the Silesian capital of Breslau' (Frederick V page). Frederick, elected king on 26 August 1619 and crowned in Prague on 4 November 1619, was put under the Imperial ban in summer 1621.

wars.name: Bohemian Revolt

zones.text: Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia, the Lands of the Bohemian Crown that Cliopatria's Habsburg Monarchy shape of 1600 holds and its shape of 1619 does not

wars.outcome: Prague's third defenestration (23 May 1618) starts the revolt; the Confederacy forms on 31 July 1619, Frederick is elected king on 26 August 1619 and crowned on 4 November 1619; Saxony backs Ferdinand for Lusatia in July 1620 and occupies it in September 1620; Ferdinand II defeats Frederick at White Mountain on 8 November 1620.
wars.note: The page's infobox dates the revolt 1618-1620 and gives no area; the span of this dossier is 1619-1620, the Confederacy's own life.

certainty.note: No page gives the Confederacy's frontier or says how much of Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia its authorities held; the lands are the Crown's, the state a fifteen-month alliance of Estates.

sources.title: Bohemian Revolt
sources.note: Third Defenestration of Prague 23 May 1618; revolt spread to all Lands of the Bohemian Crown (Bohemia, Silesia, Upper and Lower Lusatia, Moravia) and much of Upper Austria, undated; White Mountain 8 November 1620; infobox 1618-1620; no area; silent on the Confederation Act and on Lusatia's date.

notes:
Bohemian Confederacy, a rebel state written because the habsburg-monarchy dossier (Cliopatria Habsburg Monarchy, group eu-09-i) names it as counterpart; Cliopatria has no row for 1619-1620 and its Habsburg Monarchy shape of 1619 lacks the Bohemian Crown, which this dossier draws. Three pages read; the Wikipedia article Bohemian_Confederation does not exist (url_not_found).

Not settled:
- The start. The Confederacy forms on 31 July 1619 (Frederick V page); the revolt starts on 23 May 1618 (Bohemian Revolt page); the habsburg-monarchy dossier records the loss on 19 August 1619 (Thirty Years' War page). The dossier starts in July 1619.
- Extent. No page gives the lands actually held. Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia are drawn whole; much of Upper Austria joined the revolt (Bohemian Revolt page, undated) and is not drawn. Bethlen Gabor and the Hungarian front are not on the pages opened.
- Lusatia. The Thirty Years' War page has Saxony backing Ferdinand in July 1620 'in return for the cession of Lusatia', and the Electorate of Saxony page has Saxon troops occupying Lusatia in September 1620 (reviewer eu-09-i moved the loss to September); the electorate-of-saxony dossier has a Saxon occupation for the emperor from September 1620 (against habsburg-monarchy), pledge in 1623, cession 1636. This dossier follows the first and ends with a loss to electorate-of-saxony; a reviewer must reconcile the three dossiers.
- The end. The pages date only the battle (8 November 1620) and the flight (9 November); surrender of the individual lands is undated, so the loss of Moravia and Silesia is booked at the battle.
- Region names the gazetteer lacks: Lusatia (drawn as the Saxon and Brandenburg cells of the Bohemian Crown lands).
- Rulers omitted: Frederick V, elected 26 August 1619, crowned 4 November 1619, is the only name; no list.
